$comment: Canonical bookable SKU templates for Bytspot. A bookable service is not a new core noun. It is SKU + domain schema + capabilities. Webpage, Swift, and Kotlin must decode this file with default camelCase keys. Do not invent TABLE_OBJECT, MASSAGE_OBJECT, or HOTEL_OBJECT. Edit here, then update DashboardListings seeding and any native Codable/data class that vendors this catalog. v2: timing replaces the overloaded etaLabel, holdSecs makes the hold window data, and tierFloors + category ownership classify tier so price alone never demotes a cheap Platinum SKU to Green.
principle: User + Context creates Intent. Intent discovers Actionables. Actionable maps to existing ontology objects. Capabilities determine what can happen. Actions change state.
$coreNounsComment: Exactly the stable ontology: PIN, HANG, HOST, ROOM, STAY, STALL, SELLER, SKU, PERSON/CIRCLE. PASS is not here on purpose. A PASS is issued by an action and consumed by another, so it is a derived object, not a thing that is always true.
$actorComment: An entity declares what it can do, so a capability check needs an actor and not just a SKU. Without this a guest could PUBLISH. Roles are the hats one PERSON can wear; entityCapabilities is the permitted set per ontology entity. SELLER capabilities follow the doc's SELLER example plus PUBLISH from its VENDOR -> PUBLISH -> AVAILABLE example, and REFUND because only the selling side can reverse a payment.
$staffComment: A staff role is a capability subset of SELLER, never a superset: the door cannot refund and no seat can do more than the business it works for. Roles are enforced with the same canActorExecute path as entities, so the SKU state machine still has the final say. 'scope' narrows which SKUs a seat may act on and is enforced server-side; it is recorded here so every client agrees on the wording.

staffRoles.label: Manager
staffRoles.summary: Inventory, bookings and operations. No refunds.

staffRoles.label: Service provider
staffRoles.summary: Only the bookables assigned to this seat.

$sellerComment: SELLER was already a core noun with no lifecycle. This is it. A seat never exceeds the business it works for, so effective capability is the staff role intersected with what the seller's own state still allows, and a seat grants nothing at all unless it is ACTIVE. That makes 'a staff role is a subset of SELLER' true of identity too and not just of the capability list: suspending a business silences every seat inside it, including the owner's, without editing a single role. Nobody can grant a seat equal to or greater than their own, which is why seat management needs no capability of its own - it falls out of the role capability sets that already exist.

identity.$stateCapabilitiesComment: The ceiling a seller's own state puts on every seat inside it. A suspended business must still honour what it already sold, which is why CHECK_IN, VERIFY, CANCEL and REFUND survive suspension while SELL and PUBLISH do not.
identity.$requirementsComment: What must be true before a business can go live. Each names the state it blocks, so an incomplete profile reads as a checklist instead of a rejection.

seats.$grantingComment: Only an ACTIVE seat grants anything. An invite that was never accepted carries no capability, which is why INVITED is not a granting state.
seats.$ownerComment: A business always has exactly one owner seat, and it cannot be revoked because that would orphan every SKU it printed. Ownership moves by transfer, which demotes the outgoing owner in the same step.
seats.$scopeComment: An assigned-scope seat sees only the locations and bookables named on the seat. An empty assignment sees nothing rather than everything, because failing open on a scope is how a service provider ends up reading the whole business.

$tierFloorsComment: Mirrors TIER_DEFINITIONS.suggestedStartingPriceCents in DashboardListings. These are display floors and price tie-breakers, never a classifier on their own: category ownership is checked first so a $12 Parking stall stays Platinum.
$timingComment: etaKind names what the label means so clients stop guessing: readiness (space becomes usable), dispatch (someone comes to you), hold (inventory is held), nextSlot (next appointment opening), policy (fixed clock time), none (Green never dispatches). holdSecs is the machine-readable hold; RESERVED -> PUBLISHED returns an expired hold to inventory.
$discoverComment: The consumer lens. A Discover category is not the product: the SKU underneath it is. Categories are keyed by the CardType ids the rail already ships with, so this contract describes the live rail rather than a second one. A category may span domains, which is how Cottage sits under Services. Every category must resolve to bookable inventory and every domain must be reachable from a category, or the rail shows a dead tab or hides a vendor's supply.
$feedComment: minimumFeedCount is how many cards a rail must show before starter filler stops. The native client reads it from here instead of keeping its own list, because the two drifted once already and the Services rail silently lost its feed.
$availabilityComment: Availability is the printer's multiplier: one Bookable times one slot times a quantity is how many SKUs exist. A slot is not a SKU and never holds a booking, it holds capacity. remaining = quantity - committed, where committed counts only SKUs in RESERVED or CONFIRMED, so an expiring hold returns capacity instead of stranding it. slotKind is separated from slotMinutes for the same reason etaKind was split off the ETA string: a nightly stay, a rolling table and a fixed door time are three different shapes, not one number.
$locationsComment: A Location is not a new core noun. It is a PIN a SELLER holds: the same PIN a guest is sent to. Its kind decides who travels, which is what etaKind was already describing from the other end - dispatch only makes sense when the vendor moves, and a readiness ETA only makes sense when the guest does. A Bookable must sit at an ACTIVE Location before it can print anything, so an address is a publish requirement rather than a profile detail.

locations.$etaComment: The cross-check that keeps timing and geography honest. A template that promises a dispatch ETA cannot live in a domain that only ever operates from a fixed address, and a guest is never quoted travel time to a provider who is coming to them.
locations.$domainComment: The first kind is the default the wizard offers. A spa is fixed but a mobile masseuse is visiting, and a farm stand is fixed while a handyman is visiting, so wellness and green carry both rather than being forced into one.

$demandComment: Demand is the other half of the printer. A guest states an unresolved need and it stays unresolved until real capacity can absorb it, so a match is never a category guess: it must name the slot that would fill it. Demand no Bookable can answer is the vendor's most valuable signal, which is why every rule carries the reason it failed instead of silently dropping the row.

demand.$rulesComment: Ordered and named so each one is implemented and testable. capacity is last because it is the expensive rule and the only one that reads availability; it is also the only rule that can turn a plausible match into no match at all.

templates.name: Private transfer
templates.hook: A seat in a car that comes to you.
templates.title: Private airport transfer
templates.description: One car, one route, one price. Dispatch is a real ETA because a driver is actually moving toward the pickup.
actionables: Meet the driver at the PIN

templates.name: Car rental
templates.hook: The car is the STALL. Renting it is the SKU.
templates.title: Car rental day
templates.description: One day with a named vehicle. Pickup is a readiness window, not a dispatch: the car waits for the renter.

templates.name: Private coffee room
templates.hook: A cafe sells time in a room, not just a cup.
templates.title: Private room, 2 hours
templates.description: Two hours in a closed room for up to six. The room is the inventory; the coffee is not what is being booked.
templates.tagline: Two hours, six seats, one door.

timing.etaLabel: Next slot at the top of the hour

templates.name: Reserved table
templates.hook: A seat you know is there when you arrive.
templates.title: Reserved cafe table
templates.description: A held table for two. Green tier never dispatches, so this promises a seat and nothing about travel time.

templates.name: Personal shopping
templates.hook: The appointment is the SKU. The handbag is not.
templates.title: Personal shopping session
templates.description: Ninety minutes with a stylist. Merchandise stays separate: this books a person's time, not a product.

templates.name: General admission
templates.hook: A ticket is a SKU that ends in a PASS.
templates.title: General admission
templates.description: One entry. The PASS reaching ADMITTED at the door is the fulfillment event, so no separate ticket object is needed.

templates.name: VIP package
templates.hook: Same door, different PASS.
templates.title: VIP event package
templates.description: Reserved seating and host contact for a party of four. Black tier because the category and the price both say so.

templates.name: Private training
templates.hook: An hour of a trainer is the unit.
templates.title: Private training, 60 min
templates.description: Sixty minutes, one person, one trainer. Scheduled against the trainer's own calendar rather than the floor's.

templates.name: Group class
templates.hook: One class, many seats, each seat a SKU.
templates.title: Group class seat
templates.description: One seat in a scheduled class. Green tier never dispatches, so the class time is the only promise.

templates.name: Table for 2
templates.hook: Two seats. One check.
templates.title: Table for 2
templates.description: Reserved table for two. Confirm holds the seats; the host can invite one guest after.

templates.name: Table for 4
templates.hook: Friday night, four friends, one table.
templates.title: Table for 4
templates.description: Reserved table for four. Party size is the constraint; Circle invite follows confirm.
actionables: Find tables for 4 nearby right now

templates.name: Booth
templates.hook: A booth, not a new object.
templates.title: Booth for 6
templates.description: Reserved booth. Same SKU as a table, with booth schema and a larger party cap.

templates.name: Patio table
templates.hook: The patio is the hang.
templates.title: Patio table
templates.description: Outdoor patio table. Same dining SKU with patio schema — weather is context, not a new noun.

templates.name: Private dining
templates.hook: One room. Your people. The table is the hang.
templates.title: Private dining room
templates.description: Private dining room for a hosted table. SKU carries BOOK; HOST carries INVITE and VERIFY.

templates.name: Chef's table
templates.hook: The kitchen is the room.
templates.title: Chef's table
templates.description: Chef's table seating. Same dining SKU, chefs-table schema, hosted verify at the pass.

templates.name: Guest list
templates.hook: A name on the door. Not a new object.
templates.title: Guest list
templates.description: Named guest-list entry. RSVP issues a PASS; HOST VERIFY admits. No table SKU required.

templates.name: Lounge
templates.hook: A lounge seat, same SKU.
templates.title: Lounge seating
templates.description: Lounge seating for a small circle. Nightlife schema on a SKU, not a lounge object.

templates.name: VIP table
templates.hook: VIP is a schema, not a new noun.
templates.title: VIP table
templates.description: VIP table for the night. SKU with vip schema; HOST VERIFY on the PASS.

templates.name: Bottle service
templates.hook: The bottle is the SKU. The booth is the room.
templates.title: Bottle service
templates.description: Hosted bottle service. SKU settles the table; PASS admits the Circle; HOST VERIFY at the rope.

templates.name: Reserved parking
templates.hook: The stall is the plan.
templates.title: Reserved parking spot
templates.description: Guaranteed stall at the PIN. STALL stays a core noun; this template only fills the SKU that sells it.
templates.tagline: A named stall. Skip the circling.

templates.name: Valet arrival
templates.hook: Hand off the keys. The stall is still the stall.
templates.title: Valet arrival
templates.description: Valet handoff at the PIN. Automotive valet schema on a STALL SKU — not a valet object.

templates.name: 60-min massage
templates.hook: An appointment is a SKU with a clock.
templates.title: 60-minute massage
templates.description: Sixty-minute massage appointment. Wellness schema, SCHEDULE + BOOK, no new massage object.

templates.name: Private spa
templates.hook: The suite is a ROOM. The treatment is the SKU.
templates.title: Private spa suite
templates.description: In-suite spa appointment. Wellness schema on a SKU bound to a ROOM, not a spa object.

templates.name: Hotel room
templates.hook: STAY is already a noun. This only sells it.
templates.title: Hotel room night
templates.description: One night STAY. Hotel schema on the existing STAY noun — check-in is CHECK_IN, not a hotel object.

templates.name: Local service
templates.hook: Neighborhood maker. Same SKU printer.
templates.title: Neighborhood service
templates.description: Cottage-industry SKU. Green tier, local-service schema. No ETA field — Green does not dispatch.
